- **Standing rule: A `{ workspace = true }` in-tree dep needs a hand-written `dependsOn`; a
  `path =` dep needs none. Neither `dependsOn` nor `^:build` selects a downstream — only task
  `inputs` confer affectedness.**
  Moon 2.5.3's Rust toolchain resolves `path = "…"` Cargo deps into the project graph **automatically**
  (`moon query projects` labels them `source=implicit`), but does **not** resolve `workspace = true`
  inheritance. So a `{ workspace = true }` in-tree dep — the repo's default form — **must** be
  hand-declared in `dependsOn`, while a `path` dep needs nothing. This is why the drift was scattered
  rather than systematic, and it is the opposite of the "Cargo path deps are NOT auto-synced" claim
  that SMA-389 recorded and SMA-524 disproved. Either way the project edge alone is **not enough**:
  `dependsOn` is what `moon query projects --affected` follows, and a task-level `^:build` is what
  actually schedules the upstream's build under `moon ci --include-relations` — neither implies the
  other. `repo:affected-smoke` now asserts both generically for every crate
  (`ci/affected-graph/cargo_moon_parity.py`), so a new in-tree dep that forgets either one reds CI
  instead of silently under-building (SMA-524).
  Neither is enough on its own either: task `inputs` are the **only** thing that confers
  affectedness in Moon 2.5.3. `dependsOn` and `^:build` schedule an upstream's build but never
  **select** a downstream — a dependent runs only if independently affected. `--include-relations`
  is very nearly, but no longer entirely, inert: re-measured at the full 27-target shape on 2.5.3
  (SMA-595) it selects exactly ONE task the same command without it does not,
  `paigasus-kernel-py:build` — 44 RunTasks against 43, stable across repeated runs. On 2.3.2 the
  two sets were byte-identical (SMA-528). One added `build` is NOT a dependent closure, so the rule
  above still holds; do not read the flag as a working cascade. **Re-run that A/B on the next moon
  bump** — the delta moved once and can move again. Every Rust crate therefore
  declares its transitive upstream sources in `fileGroups.upstreams`, consumed by build/test/lint via
  `@group(upstreams)` in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml`. Omitting the group is a hard graph-load error
  (`project::unknown_file_group`) for every moon command; mis-declaring it reds
  `repo:affected-smoke`'s A6 — and **nothing else can**, because a crate's own `moon.yml` is not an
  input to its tasks, so a wrong group otherwise serves a cached PASS. `^:build` has a second job
  here: it orders `contracts:generate` before a downstream that keys on
  `paigasus-proto/src/generated/**`, so removing it as "vestigial" would make those cache keys
  nondeterministic.
- Broad `inputs: ['**/*']` Moon tasks (e.g. `repo:actionlint`) stay cheap only because
  `.moon/workspace.yml`'s `hasher.ignorePatterns` filters gitignored trees out of the hash walk.
- **Standing rule: What makes a contracts change select the service tests is
  `@group(upstreams)`, not `^:build`.**
  Adding a **new error-code emission site** in Rust reds `repo:error-code-single-site` until the file
  is added to `ci/error-registry/check.py`'s `MANIFEST` — as `emits` (which also requires a
  membership test asserting every code it emits resolves via `ErrorReason::from_wire_reason`),
  `asserts`, or `excluded` with a stated reason. The gate matches the registry's **declared**
  vocabulary, so it cannot see a code you invented and never added to
  `contracts/proto/paigasus/common/v1/error.proto`; adding the code there is what makes it
  resolvable on any consumer. Code **removal** needs no gate — both service crates carry
  `test: deps: ['^:build']`, so a contracts change already runs their membership tests.
  (Until SMA-528 this was aspirational: `^:build` schedules an upstream's build, it does not make a
  crate affected. What makes it true is `@group(upstreams)` — both service crates' `test` now key on
  `paigasus-proto`'s sources, so a contracts change that regenerates them selects the test.)

## Registering a new `repo:*` gate

- A new `repo:*` gate reds `:affected-smoke` until it is in **both** `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` array and
  the marker-delimited command above — `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py` asserts the two agree, and
  that every `T` entry still resolves to a CI-eligible task. That last half matters because
  `moon ci` exits **0** on a target that resolves to nothing (even with real targets around it), so
  a typo is otherwise a silent no-op on every PR. A gate that must stay out of `T` needs a
  `T_EXEMPT` entry with a reason — `runInCI: false` is NOT a general escape, since Moon then drops
  the task from `moon run` under `CI=true` too (see the comments in `ts/moon.yml`). `T` must also
  stay a single-line bash array (SMA-541).
- `repo:actionlint` and `repo:affected-smoke` now **guard each other**, and neither can guard
  itself (SMA-542). `ci/actionlint/run.sh`'s check 8 asserts `:affected-smoke` is still in
  `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` array, that no `moon` line discards its exit status (a `||`/`&&`/`;`/`|`
  tail), and that no step's `continue-on-error:` value suppresses it (anything but the literal
  `false`) — escape-hatched per line via `COE_SKIP`, keyed by BOTH the line number and the line's
  own text, so a shifted entry stops matching instead of silently absorbing a different occurrence
  that lands on the vacated line. In return, `ci_targets.py`'s `ACTIONLINT_SH_CALL_SITES` pins
  `run_self_tests` and `selftest_mutation_battery` as **whole lines** in `run.sh` (a substring
  match would survive deleting the call, since the name is a prefix of its own definition). That
  pin only works because `repo:affected-smoke` lists `ci/actionlint/**/*` in its `inputs` — remove
  that and the pin stays green on exactly the PR that breaks it. Adding a seventeenth-and-later
  `*_self_test` table means bumping `SELF_TEST_COUNT` (currently 16 — SMA-579 added the eleventh,
  `release_guard_self_test` at check 10, SMA-601 the twelfth, `cargo_lock_step_self_test` at
  check 8f, SMA-603 the thirteenth, `release_plan_self_test` at check 11, SMA-597 the
  fourteenth, `doc_diagnosis_self_test` at check 12, and SMA-647 the fifteenth,
  `early_exit_reader_self_test` at check 13, and SMA-612 the sixteenth,
  `pipe_capacity_self_test` (the full-gate preflight)): the gate asserts
  invocations AND definitions. The cycle's
  second half is now closed too (SMA-542 residual closure): check 8c
  in `ci/actionlint/run.sh` pins `ci/affected-graph/run.sh`'s own two call sites into
  `ci_targets.py`, mirroring `ci_targets.py`'s `RUN_SH_CALL_SITES` from the other, independently
  scheduled file — see `ci/actionlint/README.md`'s Limitations section (L6) for what residual
  still remains (a single combined edit deleting both gates' own call sites at once, the same
  bounded shape as the `T`-array cycle above).
- **Standing rule: A new gate of this shape carries five registry obligations. Not all five are
  self-enforcing — the `repo:ruff-ci` entry below holds the measured list.**
  `repo:workflow-credentials` (SMA-593) asserts that no `pull_request`/`pull_request_target`
  workflow **declares** a credential — a `secrets` key, `id-token: write`, `permissions:
  write-all`, or a `secrets` context read. It says nothing about whether one could **obtain**
  a credential by another path; the README's Non-goals list those, and no control in this repo
  audits per-scope `permissions:` breadth (`repo:actionlint` does not, and zizmor is named in
  prose but runs nowhere). A new gate of this shape carries **five** registry obligations, and
  missing any one of them reds `:affected-smoke`, not this gate: `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` array, the
  marker-delimited command above, `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES` (its four `moon.yml` lines —
  `set -euo pipefail`, `--self-test`, `--negative-control`, the real run),
  `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` (both literal `inputs`), and
  `T_AFFECTED_SMOKE_REQUIRED_INPUTS` in `ci/actionlint/run.sh`, which floors
  `ci/workflow-credentials/**/*` among `:affected-smoke`'s own inputs — without that last one
  the script pin below stays green on exactly the PR that breaks it.
  (Correction, SMA-539: "missing any one of them reds `:affected-smoke`" overstates it —
  `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES` and `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` validate only entries already present as
  KEYS, so omitting either one was never self-enforcing on its own; see the `repo:ruff-ci` entry
  below for the measurement and the partial fix.)
  `WORKFLOW_CREDENTIALS_SH_CALL_SITES` pins **seven** lines in `run.sh`, and three of them are the
  ASSERTION: with only the flag parse, the dispatch arm and the two report lines pinned,
  deleting every `_expect` and `grep` row left all four byte-identical and the control exited 0
  having asserted nothing (MEASURED). SMA-647 split the one assertion line into three: the capture
  of the real run, the guard on its exit status, and the match. The old pipe failed OPEN when the
  checker failed, so deleting the status guard alone is a regression, and it is pinned too.
  The **exit codes differ between the checker and the wrapper, deliberately**:
  `workflow_credentials.py` exits **3** for an assertion failure, and `run.sh` maps 3 -> 1 and
  everything else -> 2. `uv` itself exits 1 on a failed resolution, so a shared code would let
  a PyPI outage read as "a workflow declares a credential". Do not "normalize" the checker to 1.
  `EXPECTED_PR_SUBJECTS` is a **hand-maintained strict-equality** pin of the seven subject
  filenames — a new `pull_request`-triggered workflow reds this gate until someone adds it,
  which is the point, so re-baseline it deliberately rather than loosening the comparison.
- **Standing rule: Registration is seven obligations. Only T-membership, the CLAUDE.md mirror
  and — once `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES` holds a key — `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` are self-enforcing.
  A brand-new gate with no registry entries at all still passes.**
  `repo:ruff-ci` (SMA-539) lints `ci/**/*.py` against `py/pyproject.toml`'s rule set — a new `ci/`
  Python file must pass it. It routes through `uv run --locked --project py` rather than a
  dedicated uv project: `repo:actionlint`'s `inputs: ['**/*']` strictly supersets `repo:ruff-ci`'s,
  so the `py` environment is materialised once per CI run regardless of which task reaches it
  first — one lockfile therefore means one ruff version, shared with `py:lint`, with no second
  lockfile to drift out of step. `ruff format` is deliberately NOT gated over `ci/`: MEASURED,
  `line-length = 200` would rewrite 2,998 of ~15,600 existing lines, joining hand-wrapped lines and
  collapsing hand-aligned fixture tables in files that are roughly 60% comment by design. The
  corpus is derived with `git ls-files -- ':(glob)ci/**/*.py' 'ci/*.py'`, not the bare
  `'ci/**/*.py'` alone: git matches a pathspec's `**` without `FNM_PATHNAME`, so the literal `/` is
  still required and a top-level `ci/foo.py` would be missed — `'ci/*.py'` (its `*` spans `/`) and
  the `:(glob)`-magic form each independently fix it, and the gate keeps both, which is mutually
  redundant and deliberately so.
  **Registration is seven obligations, not six** — `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` array, the CLAUDE.md
  marker-delimited command, `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES`, `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS`, a script pin
  (`RUFF_SH_CALL_SITES`, ten lines), `REQUIRED_REPO_TASKS` — the last because this gate
  carries a `--negative-control`, the same reasoning that put the three `release-parity*` tasks
  and `workflow-credentials` on that floor — and `moon.yml`'s `repo:affected-smoke` task listing
  `ci/ruff/**/*` among its own `inputs` (`moon.yml:222-226`), floored by a
  `T_AFFECTED_SMOKE_REQUIRED_INPUTS` entry in `ci/actionlint/run.sh` (`:2134-2138`) — the same
  reachability pair the `workflow-credentials` entry above names for that gate: without it, a PR
  editing `ci/ruff/**` does not schedule `repo:affected-smoke` at all, so none of the other six
  obligations' pins can ever fire on the PR that breaks them.
  **This also corrects a belief this repo has been operating on.** MEASURED: `repo:affected-smoke`
  does NOT red when a brand-new `repo:*` gate is added to `ci.yml`'s `T` array with none of the
  other obligations done at all. `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES`, `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` and
  `REQUIRED_REPO_TASKS` are hand-maintained tables that validate only entries already present as
  KEYS — so a brand-new gate with NO entries at all in any of the three still passes, the same
  true statement the `workflow-credentials` entry above makes for its own registration. That is
  narrower than it first looks, though: `orphan_globs` is not "a key with no task" (nothing there
  needs a task) but a `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` KEY with no matching `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES`
  entry — i.e. the reverse-pairing direction — and `check_registry_pairing` (called with all-`None`
  at `ci_targets.py:2647`, which resolves to the LIVE registries) genuinely IS exercised in
  production: it runs on the `--self-test` path that `repo:affected-smoke`'s own
  `--negative-control` invokes (`ci/affected-graph/run.sh:413`), so deleting only
  `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES["ruff-ci"]` reds it. Obligation 4 (`SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS`) is
  therefore transitively self-enforcing once obligation 3 (`SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES`) is in place —
  it is `REQUIRED_REPO_TASKS` and the reachability pair above that remain unpaired, so of the
  seven, T-membership, the CLAUDE.md mirror, and (once `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES` exists)
  `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` are self-enforcing; the `workflow-credentials` entry above overstated
  the ORIGINAL claim ("missing any one of them reds `:affected-smoke`") and is corrected there.
  SMA-539 closes part of the remaining gap with `check_self_scheduled_coverage` in
  `ci_targets.py`: every `repo:*` task whose resolved `script:` mentions `--self-test` or
  `--negative-control` must now have a `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES` entry, with a reasoned
  `SELF_SCHEDULED_COVERAGE_EXEMPT` table that ships EMPTY. It is deliberately scoped to that ONE
  registry — the same treatment for `SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` or `REQUIRED_REPO_TASKS` would red
  the real repo, since several tasks legitimately lack those (`affected-smoke`'s own globs are
  pinned by check 8e instead; the three `release-parity*` tasks route through
  `SELF_TASK_GLOBS_EXEMPT`).
- `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py` derives its verdict AND its report from ONE list (SMA-638).
  `collect_findings` returns 23 `(key, rows, title)` triples; `main()` reads
  `if not any(rows for _, rows, _ in findings)` for the verdict and iterates that same list for the
  report, so a check folded into one and not the other cannot exist — the defect SMA-638 reported
  for `check_tailwind_guard_invocations`, which applied to every check in the file. What stops the
  list being SHRUNK is `EXPECTED_FINDING_KEYS`, a 23-key tuple whose non-emptiness, arity and exact
  key sequence `self_test()` asserts. So adding or removing a check reds the gate until that tuple
  is re-baselined, and the re-baseline is a deliberate act, never a mechanical edit to clear a red.
  The floor proves MEMBERSHIP, not semantics: a key whose `rows` are always empty satisfies it.
  Separately, `RUN_SH_CALL_SITES` (in that file) and `T_AFFECTED_GRAPH_CALL_SITES` (in
  `ci/actionlint/run.sh`) now hold **four** entries each, not two — the two `ci_targets.py`
  invocations, plus `ci/affected-graph/run.sh`'s `--negative-control` flag parse and its `NEGATIVE`
  branch guard, because `run.sh` initialises `NEGATIVE=0` and deleting either line let the control
  fall through and run the real suite twice at exit 0. The two tables are hand-mirrored and
  **nothing asserts the copies agree**, so every edit to one must be made to the other. Both are
  SUBSTRING pins (`site not in run_sh_text`; `grep -qF`): MEASURED, deleting a pinned line reds both
  gates, but COMMENTING IT OUT leaves both green. That is the documented limit
  (`ci/affected-graph/README.md`, L2), not a defect.

## Workflow linting and shell rules

- Workflow trigger filters are gated by `repo:actionlint`. Write `branches:`, `paths:` **and their
  `-ignore` variants** as **block sequences**, never the inline `branches: [main]` form — the
  gate's extractor does not parse inline flow and fails all four keys loudly rather than skipping
  them in silence. Every wildcard-free
  `branches:` entry must resolve as `refs/remotes/origin/<name>`; a branch that does not exist yet,
  or any entry carrying a glob character (`*`, `?`, `+`, `[]` — `+` included, since GitHub reads it
  as a quantifier), needs a justified `BRANCH_SKIP` entry in `ci/actionlint/run.sh`. A typo'd
  branch name otherwise disables a workflow silently and permanently (SMA-540).
- `ci/actionlint/run.sh`'s check 10 must route **every** exit status of its `release_guard_py`
  wrapper, not only the guard's own 2. `run.sh` is `set -uo pipefail` with **no `-e`**, so an
  unrouted status leaves `$RG_OUT` empty, the read loop finds nothing and the gate exits 0 having
  asserted nothing — measured at rc 127, the status a **missing `uv`** produces from the wrapper
  rather than from the guard. Do not read "missing uv aborts the gate" as a property of this
  routing: on the full-gate path that abort comes from `release_guard_self_test`'s
  `|| infra`. The wrapper also passes `--locked`, so the gate cannot re-lock `py/uv.lock` as a
  side effect (SMA-579).
- PyYAML coerces five shapes every workflow parser in `ci/` must handle: a bare `on:` key parses
  as the boolean `True`; `if: false` and `continue-on-error: false` parse as the boolean `False`;
  `continue-on-error: "false"` (quoted) parses as the **string** `"false"`, not the boolean;
  `needs:` may be a scalar string rather than a list, and iterating a string in Python yields its
  **characters**, not the string itself (SMA-579).
- GitHub Actions supports YAML **anchors and aliases** (since 2025-09-18) but **not merge keys**
  (`<<:`) — a workflow using one keeps the literal, unmerged key rather than erroring (SMA-579).
- `repo:actionlint` now runs shellcheck over every workflow `run:` block, sourced from
  `shellcheck-py` pinned in `py/uv.lock` (bounded specifier `>=0.11.0.1,<0.12`), resolved via
  `uv run --locked --project py` and asserted with `[ -x ]`. It FAILS CLOSED at rc 2 — there is
  deliberately no fallback to whatever `shellcheck` a host happens to have, the silent-downgrade
  failure SMA-525 refused. shellcheck's own GitHub release ships 13 platform archives and no
  checksums asset (re-measured 2026-09-02), which is why it is not a proto plugin; three of
  `shellcheck-py`'s pinned digests were verified by hand against koalaman's release assets, and a
  version bump re-opens that check.
  **Coverage limit, stated plainly so "the inline bash is linted now" isn't read as more than it
  is.** MEASURED: actionlint replaces `${{ }}` expressions with inert placeholders before handing
  the script to shellcheck. `rm -rf $TARGET` fires `SC2086`; the structurally identical
  `rm -rf ${{ github.event.inputs.target }}` fires nothing. So the entire GitHub-expression
  interpolation class — the dominant quoting/injection hazard in `release.yml` and `wheels.yml` —
  is uncovered by this gate. zizmor is the tool for that class and runs nowhere in this repo. Also
  structural, not a configuration gap: `SC2148` and `SC2164` can never fire, because actionlint
  supplies the shell itself and injects `set -e`.
- `ci/actionlint/run.sh` check 12 requires a `<!-- moon-diagnosis:ok -->` (or `:superseded`) marker
  on ANY file that names `ciReport.json`, unless the file is listed in `CIREPORT_MENTIONS_ALLOWED`.
  This is broader than the `doc_diagnosis_self_test` entry above says: it is not only about this
  file's own diagnosis procedure block. A new plan or spec that quotes the procedure, or otherwise
  mentions `ciReport.json`, reds the gate until it carries the marker or is added to the allowlist.
- **A pipe into a reader that can exit early is a false red under `pipefail`** (MEASURED, SMA-647).
  `grep -q` stops at its first match. `grep -m N` stops after N matches. `head` stops after N
  lines. `awk … exit` stops at its `exit`. Each one stops before it reads the rest of its input. A
  producer that writes again after that gets SIGPIPE and exits 141. Under `pipefail` the pipeline
  status is then 141, although the reader found the match. On Linux in CI the race is rare and
  needs CPU load, so a re-run passes: it caused three false check-12 reds in `repo:actionlint`
  (PRs 223, 255, 258). On macOS with BSD grep 2.6.0 it is near-certain: the old check-12 probe
  missed on 500 of 500 runs against the real block. Use one of three forms instead. When the
  producer's status does not
  matter, use process substitution: `grep -qF -- "$lit" < <(printf '%s' "$block")`. When the
  status matters, capture the producer into a variable, check its status, then match the variable
  the same way; declare a `local` on its own line, and under `set -e` write the capture as the left
  side of `||`. In place of `head -1` or `grep -m1 … | sed`, use `sed -n 1p`; in place of
  `awk '…{print $2; exit}'`, take the first match in awk's `END` block. Do not use a here-string:
  Homebrew bash 5.3.15 deadlocks on one over about 512 bytes (see the LOCAL ONLY entry). Do not use
  `>/dev/null` in place of `-q`, and do not use a `sed` script with `q`. `ci/actionlint/run.sh`
  check 13 bans the pattern in every tracked `*.sh`, workflow, `moon.yml`, `.moon/**/*.yml` and
  `lefthook.yml`. The rule reads only the next command word after the pipe, so a reader inside a
  subshell or a brace group, a reader behind a wrapper word, and a `|&` pipe are not seen — see
  `ci/actionlint/README.md` L33–L41. Its allowlist, `EARLY_EXIT_READER_ALLOWED`, ships empty. Its
  fixtures live in `ci/actionlint/fixtures/early-exit/*.txt`, because check 13 also scans
  `run.sh`. Check 12 keeps
  a second opinion on each missing literal: a `literal-disagreement` row means `grep` and a bash
  `case` match disagree, which is evidence of a second mechanism. Keep that run's whole output for
  SMA-647 before you re-run.
- `crane config` accepts a **registry reference only**. MEASURED against crane 0.22.1:
  `crane config "oci-archive:in/paigasus-iam-amd64.oci.tar"` fails with `Error: fetching config:
  parsing reference … could not parse reference`, and with a missing file it tries to resolve a
  host named `oci-archive`. `oci-archive:` is a syft/skopeo transport, not a crane one. Read an
  image config from a local archive with `ci/images/release_decision.py labels <archive>` instead
  (SMA-658 C1); it prints `version=` and `revision=` from the same labels.

## Fixture git repositories: no background maintenance (SMA-708)

- A fixture repository under `ci/` in which any process runs `git commit`, `merge`, `fetch`,
  `pull`, `am`, `rebase` or `cherry-pick`, or which receives a push, sets
  `maintenance.auto false` and `gc.auto 0` with `git config` directly after `git init`. This
  includes git calls that an external tool (release-plz, semantic-release, PSR) makes in it.
- Why: after such a command, git starts a detached `git maintenance run --auto`. It writes
  `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` while the fixture's `shutil.rmtree` or `rm -rf` runs. On Python
  3.12 that raced into `FileNotFoundError: 'maintenance.lock'` (7 of 2,400 runs under load).
- A fixture with only `init`, `add`, `tag`, `ls-files` or `rm --cached` needs no keys. If you add
  one of the commands above to such a fixture, add the two keys in the same edit.
- Do not hide the race with `ignore_errors=True`, a retry, or `|| true`.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-sma-708-git-maintenance-fixtures-design.md`.

## A nested `moon` call that targets a fixture workspace (SMA-714)

- A gate that runs `moon` against a DIFFERENT workspace (a throwaway fixture) runs it with an
  allowlist environment: `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" TMPDIR=… LANG=… PROTO_HOME=…
  PROTO_REPORTER=text MOON_WORKSPACE_ROOT="<fixture>"`. `ci/moon-diagnosis/run.sh` is the worked
  example.
- Why: moon passes its own `MOON_*` and `PROTO_*` variables to a task. An inherited
  `MOON_WORKSPACE_ROOT` moves the nested run to the real workspace (MEASURED: it failed with
  `app::missing_config` when the variable pointed to another directory). An inherited
  `PROTO_MOON_VERSION` overrides the fixture's `.prototools` pin, because proto reads
  `PROTO_<TOOL>_VERSION` first. One probe also printed `Base revision: N/A` under inherited `CI`
  and `GITHUB_*` variables. A second probe on 2026-09-28 with the same variable names did not
  show it, so that cause is not confirmed. `repo:moon-diagnosis-exec` asserts
  `Base revision: <sha>` on every run.
- Use an allowlist, not a denylist such as `unset MOON_*`. A new variable passes a denylist, and
  `env` output can hold multi-line values.
- This rule does NOT apply to a nested call that must target the REAL workspace, for example the
  nested `moon query` in `repo:affected-smoke`. That call needs the inherited environment.
- A fixture that commits also sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` on every
  `git` call and local `commit.gpgsign false` and `tag.gpgsign false`. The development Mac signs
  every commit through 1Password, and a locked vault makes an unguarded fixture commit hang or fail.

</system-reminder>

this shape. It is left open as scope, not as an inherent limit, so a later reader can pick it up
deliberately.

1	# SMA-765 — the kernel test uses its own virtual environment
2	
3	- Linear: SMA-765
4	- Date: 2026-11-12
5	- Status: revision 2, after the builder check and the spec challenge. For approval at GATE 1.
6	
7	## 1. Intent
8	
9	`moon ci` can fail at random in `py:test` with `ModuleNotFoundError` during test collection. The
10	failure has no relation to the change under test. It reached Dependabot PR #455 on 2026-11-12
11	(CI run 43295812102), and a re-run passed with no code change.
12	
13	The cause is one shared virtual environment, `py/.venv`, with one writer that removes packages:
14	
15	- `paigasus-kernel-py:test` (`py/packages/paigasus-kernel/moon.yml`, `test` task) runs
16	  `uv sync --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings` from the member directory. A plain
17	  `uv sync` is EXACT. It removes every package that this one member does not need. In run
18	  43295812102 it logged "Uninstalled 18 packages", `grpclib` and `anthropic` included.
19	- Readers of `py/.venv` that can run at the same time: `py:test`, `py:lint`, `py:fmt`,
20	  `py:typecheck` (`.moon/tasks/python.yml`), `paigasus-gateway-conformance:test`
21	  (`uv run pytest tests`), `contracts:generate` (`uv run --project ../py`), `repo:actionlint`
22	  and `repo:ruff-ci` (`uv run --locked --project py`), and `repo:release-parity-py`
23	  (`uv run --frozen`). `uv run` syncs INEXACTLY by default, so these tasks only add packages.
24	
25	When Moon runs the kernel test at the same time as a reader, the reader loses packages in the
26	middle of its run. `--reinstall-package` adds a second, smaller race: it removes and writes
27	`paigasus-py-bindings` again, and `py:test` also collects `packages/paigasus-kernel/tests`,
28	which import that binding.
29	
30	## 2. Decision
31

35	runs `uv run --isolated`. uv then makes a temporary environment in its cache directory, uses
36	it for this one run, and deletes it. The task no longer runs `uv sync`. The kernel test does

# SMA-765 — the kernel test uses its own virtual environment

- Linear: SMA-765
- Date: 2026-11-12
- Status: revision 2, after the builder check and the spec challenge. For approval at GATE 1.

## 1. Intent

`moon ci` can fail at random in `py:test` with `ModuleNotFoundError` during test collection. The
failure has no relation to the change under test. It reached Dependabot PR #455 on 2026-11-12
(CI run 43295812102), and a re-run passed with no code change.

The cause is one shared virtual environment, `py/.venv`, with one writer that removes packages:

- `paigasus-kernel-py:test` (`py/packages/paigasus-kernel/moon.yml`, `test` task) runs
  `uv sync --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings` from the member directory. A plain
  `uv sync` is EXACT. It removes every package that this one member does not need. In run
  43295812102 it logged "Uninstalled 18 packages", `grpclib` and `anthropic` included.
- Readers of `py/.venv` that can run at the same time: `py:test`, `py:lint`, `py:fmt`,
  `py:typecheck` (`.moon/tasks/python.yml`), `paigasus-gateway-conformance:test`
  (`uv run pytest tests`), `contracts:generate` (`uv run --project ../py`), `repo:actionlint`
  and `repo:ruff-ci` (`uv run --locked --project py`), and `repo:release-parity-py`
  (`uv run --frozen`). `uv run` syncs INEXACTLY by default, so these tasks only add packages.

When Moon runs the kernel test at the same time as a reader, the reader loses packages in the
middle of its run. `--reinstall-package` adds a second, smaller race: it removes and writes
`paigasus-py-bindings` again, and `py:test` also collects `packages/paigasus-kernel/tests`,
which import that binding.

## 2. Decision

Sven chose option D on 2026-11-12: **the kernel test uses its own virtual environment.**

Revision 2 makes the mechanism concrete (my call after the spec challenge, see §10): the task
runs `uv run --isolated`. uv then makes a temporary environment in its cache directory, uses
it for this one run, and deletes it. The task no longer runs `uv sync`. The kernel test does
not read or write `py/.venv` at all, and no environment directory appears in the repo tree.

## 3. Goals

- G1. The kernel test task does not remove, add or reinstall any package in `py/.venv`.
- G2. `paigasus-kernel-py:test` keeps its current guarantee: it tests a binding that is built
  from the current Rust source (`touch` + `--reinstall-package`, SMA-420 / SMA-430).
- G3. A gate fails if any Moon task mutates a uv project environment in place again.

## 4. Non-goals and residuals

- N1. No change to task ordering, task `deps`, the affected graph, or `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- N2. No change to how `py/uv.lock` is written. Today `uv sync` may relock; `uv run` has the same
  default. No `--locked` or `--frozen` is added (`ci/version-lockstep/README.md:25` documents the
  current behavior).
- R-stale. **Residual, a behavior change on a developer machine.** Today the kernel task also
  refreshes the binding in `py/.venv` as a side effect. After this change nothing does: a bare
  `uv run` serves the cached wheel and does not see Rust changes (measured,
  `ci/affected-graph/run.sh:402-406`). So `py:test` and `py:typecheck` can run the kernel tests
  and the stub against an old binding after a Rust edit. Remedy, to run when no Moon run is
  active: `(cd py && uv sync --all-packages --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings)`. The PR
  adds this line to `py/README.md` or the nearest Python CLAUDE.md. Rejected fix:
  `[tool.uv] cache-keys` on the Rust sources. With the kernel task's `touch`, every reader's
  `uv run` would then reinstall the binding in `py/.venv`, and the race comes back.
- R-toolchain. Moon's own `InstallDependencies(unstable_python, py)` action writes `py/.venv`.
  Every Python task depends on it, so it runs before them. Readers with the `system` toolchain
  (`repo:actionlint`, `repo:ruff-ci`) do not depend on it. Whether that is a race is not
  measured, and it is out of scope. A14 cannot see toolchain actions.
- R-relock. An inexact `uv run` still changes a package when the lock and the environment
  disagree. That is not a race between two tasks of one run, and it is out of scope.

Anti-goal: a fix that only makes the race less frequent. `--inexact` alone is such a fix (§9).

- F2. `uv run --isolated --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings …`, run from
  `py/packages/paigasus-kernel`, uses a temporary environment under the uv cache

  `uv sync --all-packages --locked`, the package list of `py/.venv` was the same before and
  after the run, and `find py/.venv -newer <marker>` found 0 files. Wall time without a Rust
  recompile: 2.5 s.
- F3. The isolated environment contains pytest (9.2.0): the root `dev` dependency group is
  installed. So `uv run --isolated … pytest tests` works without a separate sync.

  (measured with a temporary `env:` block on the kernel task). A missing `env:` block gives no
  `env` key.
- F5. The free check number in `repo:affected-smoke` is A14 (A10–A13 exist).
- F6. **Local limit on this Mac.** The binding built on this host does not load:
  `dlopen … mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool, fileOffset=0x00062514`. This happens in
  `py/.venv` and in the isolated environment, so it is not caused by this design. CI (Linux)
  runs `paigasus-kernel-py:test` green today. So the local proof (§7) measures `py/.venv`
  only, and CI proves that the kernel tests pass.

```
touch <kernel lib.rs> <binding lib.rs> && uv sync --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings && uv run pytest tests

- Keep the inputs unchanged.

   the moon.yml change, A14 reds on the kernel task. After it, A14 is green. Run
   `/bin/bash ci/affected-graph/run.sh` directly (system bash 3.2; Moon can pick Homebrew bash
   5.3.15, which deadlocks on this Mac).
4. CI: `paigasus-kernel-py:test` and `py:test` both pass. CI is the authority for the kernel
   tests themselves (F6).

The kernel task's pytest step fails locally in both states because of F6. Steps 1 and 2 still
work, because `uv sync` / `uv run --isolated` run before pytest. Record the numbers in the PR
body.

## 8. Risks and rollback

- Cost: an isolated environment per kernel test run. Measured 2.5 s without a Rust recompile
  (F2). The maturin build costs the same as today.
- The isolated environment is in the uv cache, which CI restores and saves. uv deletes the
  temporary environment after the run.
- Rollback: revert the commit. No directory to delete.

## 9. Options that were considered

| Option | Result | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| A. `uv sync --inexact` in the shared venv | Removes the package loss | The binding reinstall still races `py:test`. The race becomes rarer, not gone (anti-goal). |
| B. A Moon `deps` edge that orders the two tasks | The pair never overlaps | It protects only the named pair. Other readers stay exposed. CI gets slower. |
| B2. A Moon `options.mutex` | Serializes the tasks that opt in | Every reader must opt in (same weakness as B), and it serializes the readers too. |
| C. One step that builds the binding for all Python tasks | Every task sees a fresh binding | Every Python task then waits for a maturin build. Task inputs and the affected graph change. |
| D1. Own venv via `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-kernel-test` (revision 1) | Isolation | A directory in the tree: Moon hashes it (`hasher.ignorePatterns` does not match it), ruff can lint it, and it needs a `.gitignore` line. |
| **D2. `uv run --isolated` (revision 2)** | Isolation, nothing in the tree | Chosen. |

## 10. Changelog of revision 2

From the spec challenge (verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES) and the builder check.

Folded in:

- BLOCKER 1 (Moon hashes the new venv; `hasher.ignorePatterns` has only `**/.venv/**`):
  removed by D2. There is no directory in the tree. This also removes the ruff and `.gitignore`
  findings.
- BLOCKER 2 (A14 match rule contradicted the helpers): §6.2 now states the scan scope, a
  fail-closed string policy and an allowlist.
- MAJOR stale binding: added as R-stale with the remedy and the rejected `cache-keys` fix.
- MAJOR "dedicated" not enforced: no longer needed. `--isolated` makes one fresh environment
  per run, so two tasks cannot share one. A14 reds any `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` use.
- MAJOR other mutating verbs, global options, overrides, script indirection: in §6.2.
- MAJOR vacuous proof: §7 now restores `py/.venv` first, uses a marker file and a deterministic
  reader.
- MINOR: `env` in `moon_projects()` (measured, F4); named floor; explicit real-tree negative
  control; `EXPECTED_FINDING_KEYS`; mutex in §9; complete reader list in §1; G1 scoped to the
  kernel task; residuals R-toolchain and R-relock; local bash note; rollback.
- Builder questions 1-7: answered by F4, §6.2, §7 and F6.

Not folded in:

- `--locked` on the kernel sync: out of scope (N2). It changes the lockfile behavior that
  `repo:version-lockstep` documents.
- A measurement of whether Moon fails on a file that disappears during the hash walk: no longer
  needed with D2.

        for off, verb, sub, flags in c._uv_invocations(blob):

import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(root / "ci" / "affected-graph"))
import cargo_moon_parity as c  # noqa: E402

cases = [
    ("gap1 new verb (hypothetical)", "uv frobnicate --sync"),
    ("gap2 default-assign", ': "${UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT:=.venv-x}"; uv run pytest'),
    ("gap2 default-assign bare", "echo ${VIRTUAL_ENV:=x}"),
    ("gap3 bare assign", "UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-x"),
    ("gap3 bare assign + newline cmd", "VIRTUAL_ENV=/x\nuv run pytest"),
    ("gap3 assign then run", "UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=x uv run pytest"),
    ("gap3 env -S", "env UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=x uv run pytest"),
    ("other: declare -x", "declare -x UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=x"),
    ("other: uv via var", 'UVB=uv; "$UVB" sync'),
    ("other: uv lock", "uv lock"),
    ("other: uv run pip install", "uv run pip install x"),
    ("other: uv run uv sync", "uv run uv sync"),
    ("other: uvx", "uvx ruff check"),
    ("other: uv tool install", "uv tool install ruff"),
    ("other: uv sync --dry-run", "uv sync --dry-run"),
    ("other: --upgrade", "uv run --upgrade pytest"),
    ("other: python -m uv", "python -m uv sync"),
    ("other: .venv pip", "py/.venv/bin/pip install x"),
    ("other: eval", "eval 'uv'' sync'"),
    ("other: printf", "$(printf u)v sync"),
]
for label, text in cases:
    try:
        r = c.uv_mutations(text)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        r = f"EXC {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    print(f"{'RED  ' if r else 'green'} {label:34} {text!r} -> {r}")

fix(py): run the kernel test in an isolated uv environment (SMA-765) (#457)

* docs(py): spec for the isolated kernel test environment (SMA-765)

The kernel test runs uv run --isolated, so it no longer syncs the shared py/.venv.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(py): implementation plan for the isolated kernel test (SMA-765)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(ci): add affected-smoke A14 for in-place uv environment writes (SMA-765)

A14 reds when a Moon task can change a uv environment in place: uv sync,
uv pip, uv venv, uv add or remove, uv run with --reinstall and no --isolated,
or any UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, VIRTUAL_ENV or --active use.
It scans the task command, followed ci scripts and project scripts.
The real tree is red on the kernel task until the task moves to uv run
--isolated. That is the red-first state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): close A14 registry and uv option gaps (SMA-765)

Add the py/scripts glob to T_AFFECTED_SMOKE_REQUIRED_INPUTS and use one
text form in moon.yml. Find the uv verb as the first known subcommand,
so an unlisted valued option cannot hide it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(py): run the kernel test in an isolated uv environment (SMA-765)

The kernel test ran an exact `uv sync` in the shared py/.venv.
It removed packages that parallel Moon tasks needed.
The test now runs `uv run --isolated --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings`.
This command does not write py/uv.lock. The docs now say so.
The README describes the stale-binding remedy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(ci): limit the uv.lock claims to the measured kernel-task fact (SMA-765)

The earlier text said that no Moon task relocks py/uv.lock.
Nobody measured that. A plain `uv run` in another task can relock it.
The text now states only the measured kernel-task result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(ci): state what version-lockstep checks in py/uv.lock (SMA-765)

The version-lockstep gate checks only the member version strings in py/uv.lock.
It does not check the rest of the lock.
Both docs now say this, and keep the measured kernel-task fact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): read ./ and ../ scripts refs in A14 and tighten its control (SMA-765)

A14 stopped reading a script named as ./scripts/x.sh. The ref pattern now accepts ./ and ../
prefixes and resolves them against the project dir. A ref that leaves the repo raises.
The real-tree negative control now needs a non-FLOOR row for the kernel task.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(ci): fix the uv.lock claims and A14 notes (SMA-765)

Name the two drifting sites, state the measured uv.lock fact, narrow the py/README claim,
split long sentences in the A14 entry and name the --upgrade limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): close four A14 parser gaps from review (SMA-765)

Treat --force-reinstall like --reinstall in the uv run rule.
Red a uv version call that sets a version unless it has --no-sync, --frozen or --dry-run.
Skip the value of a known valued uv global option before the verb is chosen.
Count --isolated only in the uv run option region, and ignore a # comment.
Note the measured lockfile result in the plan and update the A14 README entry.

"""Gap 5: is every file A14 reads matched by an input of repo:affected-smoke?"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(root / "ci" / "affected-graph"))
import cargo_moon_parity as c  # noqa: E402

projects = json.load(open(Path(__file__).parent / "projects.json"))
smoke = projects["repo"]
globs = smoke["task_input_globs"]["affected-smoke"]
files = smoke["task_inputs"]["affected-smoke"] or []
pats = [c._moon_glob_re(g) for g in globs if not g.startswith("!")]
read = set()
for pid, proj in projects.items():
    for name, blob in (proj.get("invocations") or {}).items():
        if not blob:
            continue
        t = f"{pid}:{name}"
        for ref in c.task_script_refs(projects, root, t):
            read.update(str(p.relative_to(root)) for p in c._uv_script_closure(ref, root))
        for rel in set(c.PROJECT_SCRIPT_REF_RE.findall(blob)):
            read.update(str(p.relative_to(root)) for p in c._uv_script_closure((root / proj["source_dir"] / rel).resolve(), root))
for f in sorted(read):
    ok = f in files or any(p.fullmatch(f) for p in pats)
    print("reached" if ok else "NOT REACHED", f)

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/smaschek/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/7.0.0/skills/brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |

# SMA-768 — A14: replace the uv parser with an allow-list of approved forms

- Linear: SMA-768 (follows SMA-765, PR #457, merged as `8ef62d58`)
- Date: 2026-11-13
- Status: revision 1, for approval at GATE 1. The option decision (§3) is provisional. It needs
  Sven.

## 1. Intent

SMA-765 added check A14 to `repo:affected-smoke` (`check_uv_env_isolation` in
`ci/affected-graph/cargo_moon_parity.py`). A14 reds when a Moon task can change a uv project
environment in place. Six review rounds made A14 a small shell parser: a segmenter
(`_uv_segments`), a word splitter (`_uv_words`, `_uv_tokens`), a quote tracker (`_uv_quoted_at`),
a verb finder over a closed list (`UV_SUBCOMMANDS`, `UV_GLOBAL_VALUED`, `UV_RUN_VALUED`) and three
denylists (`UV_MUTATING_VERBS`, `UV_PIP_MUTATING`, `UV_RUN_MUTATING_FLAGS`). SMA-768 lists six
gaps that this parser leaves open, and asks for one decision:

- Option 1: close the gaps that matter in the current parser.
- Option 2: replace the parser with a smaller, blunter rule: an allow-list of exact approved `uv`
  forms.

This spec measures both options on the real tree and recommends option 2.

## 2. Measured facts

All numbers are from this branch (base `8ef62d58`), measured with `moon query projects` on
moon 2.5.3 and uv 0.11.16. The scripts are in the session scratch directory. They are not
committed.

- M1. **Size of A14 today.** The parser and the check are 412 lines
  (`cargo_moon_parity.py:3225-3636`), 346 of them code. The waiver table
  `ALLOW_UV_ENV_SCRIPT` holds 4 entries. The self-test has a 61-row parser table and about 30
  check-level rows (`:6865-7070`, 206 lines).
- M2. **Scan scope today.** 171 Moon tasks have a command. A14 reads their blobs and 18 scripts
  (the `ci/**/*.sh` closure through `UV_SOURCE_STMT_RE`, plus `py/scripts/run_tests.sh`). On the
  real tree A14 gives 0 rows.
- M3. **Every executed `uv` form on the real tree.** There are 11 `uv` uses in task blobs and 17
  executed `uv` uses in the scanned scripts. They use 2 verbs and 5 options only:

  | Form | Where |
  |---|---|
  | `uv build` (no other word) | `paigasus-{kernel,ml,proto,workflows}-py:build` |
  | `uv run <cmd>` | `py:fmt`, `py:lint`, `py:typecheck` (3), `paigasus-gateway-conformance-py:test`, `py/scripts/run_tests.sh:17,32` (3) |
  | `uv run --isolated --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings pytest tests` | `paigasus-kernel-py:test` (the floor task) |
  | `uv run --locked --project <v> [--python <v>] <cmd>` | `ci/actionlint/run.sh:4619,4655,4669,5305,5982`, `ci/ruff/run.sh:90`, `ci/helm-render/run.sh:93`, `ci/wasm-lockstep/run.sh:52` |
  | `uv run --project <v> --python <v> <cmd>` | `ci/workflow-credentials/run.sh:33,70,78` |
  | `uv run --frozen <cmd>` | `ci/release-parity/ecosystems/python-semantic-release.sh:48` |
  | `uv lock` | `ci/version-lockstep/run.sh:1635`, inside `run_write`. `repo:version-lockstep` does not pass `--write`, so no Moon task runs this line. |
  | `command -v uv` (a presence probe) | `ci/helm-render/run.sh:92`, `ci/wasm-lockstep/run.sh:51`, `ci/workflow-credentials/run.sh:26` |

- M4. **The six gaps, probed on today's parser** (`uv_mutations`):

  | Gap | Probe | Today |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1. closed subcommand list | `uv frobnicate --sync` | green (missed) |
  | 2. `:=` default assignment | `echo ${VIRTUAL_ENV:=x}`, `: "${UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT:=.venv-x}"` | green (missed) |
  | 3. assignment with no command | `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-x`, `VIRTUAL_ENV=/x` + newline + `uv run pytest` | **red** (not reproduced, see P3) |
  | 4. a script that is not UTF-8 | `Path.read_text()` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` | traceback, exit 1 (reads as an assertion failure, not rc 2). `UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError`, and `INFRA_ERRORS` (`:77`) does not list it. |
  | 5. `scripts/*.sh` outside `py/` | `git ls-files` | no such `.sh` file exists today. All 18 files that A14 reads are matched by an input of `repo:affected-smoke` today. Nothing reds when a new one is not. |
  | 6. `source` text inside a quoted argument | by design | fail-closed (a false red), not a hidden mutation |

- M5. **More forms that today's parser misses** (found by the same probe):

  | Probe | Today | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | `uv lock` | green | writes `py/uv.lock`. The SMA-768 issue text says that A14 covers `py/uv.lock`. It does not. |
  | `uv run --upgrade pytest` | green | can change installed versions in place. README names it as a limit. |
  | `uv tool install ruff` | green | writes the uv tool directory, not a project environment |
  | `uv run pip install x` | green | can write `py/.venv` when pip is in it |
  | `UVB=uv; "$UVB" sync`, `$(printf u)v sync` | green | uv through a variable or a computed word |
  | `py/.venv/bin/pip install x` | green | a direct write that does not use uv |

- M6. **Option 2 on the real tree** (a prototype of §4.2, measurement only). Every executed form
  in M3 is green, except `uv lock` at `ci/version-lockstep/run.sh:1635`. 27 physical lines are
  red. 26 of them only name `uv` in a message, a `printf`, a `grep` pattern or Python data
  (for example `die_infra "uv is not on PATH …"` and `ws.get("tool", {}).get("uv", {})`). Of
  today's 4 waivers, 3 are among the 27. The fourth
  (`python-semantic-release.sh:34`) is a full-line comment, which option 2 does not scan, so it
  goes away. So the waiver table grows from 4 to 27 entries: 26 message or data lines and the
  `uv lock` line.
- M7. **Option 2 on today's 61 parser rows.** All 47 red rows stay red. 14 green rows turn red,
  because they are not an approved form: the six `uv version` rows,
  `uv run --isolated --force-reinstall pytest`, `uv --directory sync run pytest`, four
  `--isolated` rows with an option or package that is not approved, `echo uv run's own status`,
  and `touch a b && uv run --isolated --reinstall-package p pytest tests` (`p` is not
  `paigasus-py-bindings`). None of the 14 forms occurs on the real tree.
- M8. **The real-tree negative control under option 2.** Remove `--isolated` from the kernel
  task. The prototype gives a row for `paigasus-kernel-py:test`
  (`--reinstall-package without --isolated`).
- M9. **Change rate of the lines that option 2 waives.** Since 2026-08-01, 16 of the 44 commits
  that touched the scanned scripts changed a line that names `uv`. That is an upper bound on how
  often a waiver must be re-keyed. Not every such commit touches a waived line.

## 3. Decision (provisional — needs Sven)

**Recommendation: option 2.** My call, for Sven to confirm or overturn at GATE 1.

Reasons:

1. The real need is small. The real tree uses 2 verbs and 5 options (M3). A short allow-list
   covers all of it, and anything else reds until a person approves it.
2. Option 2 fails closed by construction. Gap 1, `uv lock`, `--upgrade`, `uv tool` and every
   future uv verb or flag are red with no extra rule. Option 1 must add each one to a denylist,
   and a form that nobody added stays green (M4, M5).
3. The parser goes away. About 346 code lines and their 61-row table become about 100 lines
   (an estimate, not a measurement). The six review rounds of SMA-765 were spent on the
   parser's corner cases.

Costs of option 2, stated plainly:

- C1. The waiver table grows from 4 to 27 entries (M6). A change to a waived line reds A14 until
  the entry is re-keyed. M9 gives the upper bound on the rate.
- C2. 14 synthetic forms that are green today become red (M7). A future task that needs one of
  them must add it to the allow-list, with a self-test row.
- C3. Option 2 does not see more than option 1 in two places: uv through a variable (M5) and a
  mutating command that `uv run` executes (`uv run pip install`). Both options miss these.

Option 1, for comparison: keep the parser. Pin `UV_SUBCOMMANDS` to the uv version in
`.prototools`, so a uv bump reds until a person reviews the list (gap 1). Add a `:=` pattern
(gap 2). Add `lock`, `tool`, `--upgrade` and `--upgrade-package` to the denylists (M5). Gaps 4
and 5 are fixed the same way as in option 2 (§4.3). Estimated cost: about 40 more code lines and
about 12 more rows, on top of the 346-line parser. Each new uv form after that is green until a
person adds it.

## 4. Design (option 2)

### 4.1 What stays

- The scan scope: the task blob (A5's `invocations`), the `ci/**/*.sh` scripts from
  `task_script_refs`, the project `scripts/*.sh` files from `PROJECT_SCRIPT_REF_RE`, and the
  `source` closure of each through `_uv_script_closure` and `UV_SOURCE_STMT_RE`.
- `SOURCE_STMT_RE` and `task_script_closure` do not change. A8 and A10 follow exactly what they
  follow today.
- The task `env:` rule: a task `env:` that sets `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` or `VIRTUAL_ENV` is a
  row.
- `ALLOW_UV_ENV_SCRIPT`: keyed by (script path, exact stripped line), with a non-empty reason.
  An empty reason is a row. A stale entry is a row. Blob lines cannot be waived.
- `REQUIRED_UV_ISOLATED_TASKS = ("paigasus-kernel-py:test",)` and its `FLOOR:` rows.
- The real-tree negative control in `main()`, unchanged in behavior: remove `--isolated` from the
  floor task in a deep copy. Exit 2 unless A14 gives a row that names the task and is not a
  `FLOOR:` row.
- The findings key `a14` and its place in `EXPECTED_FINDING_KEYS`.

### 4.2 The new rule

Read each scanned text as logical lines. A `\` at the end of a line joins the next line. Report a
row at the physical line of the match.

1. **Comment lines.** Skip a logical line whose first non-blank character is `#`. Do not skip a
   `#` later in a line: `x # uv sync` stays a hit (fail-closed).
2. **Every `uv` token is checked.** A `uv` token is `UV_TOKEN_RE` (unchanged:
   `(?<![\w.-])uv(?![\w.-])`). Every match in a non-comment line must be an approved form, or
   the line is a row. A match inside a quoted string is checked too: `bash -c "uv sync"` and
   `"$(uv run …)"` execute.
3. **One invocation.** The text after the match ends at the first `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `)` or
   backtick. This cut is not quote-aware, on purpose. Split the rest on whitespace.
4. **Approved forms.** Nothing else is approved.
   - A1. `uv build` with no further word.
   - A2. `uv run`, then zero or more approved options, then a command word.
     - Approved flags: `--locked`, `--frozen`, `--isolated`.
     - Approved valued options: `--project <v>`, `--python <v>`. The value is the next word.
       The `--opt=value` form is not approved.
     - `--reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings` is approved only when `--isolated` is in the
       same option region.
     - The option region ends at the first word that does not start with `-`. That word is the
       command word. A2 with no command word is red.
   - A3. `command -v uv`, with only redirections after it in the invocation.
5. **Word shape.** Each option value and the command word must be a plain word: letters, digits,
   `_ . / = < > @ : + -`, a `$NAME` or `${NAME}` expansion, or a complete `'…'` or `"…"` string
   with no space inside. A word with an unbalanced quote, `$(`, a backtick or a `\` is red. This
   makes every parse confusion red. Example: in `uv run --project "a b" --reinstall pytest`, the
   value `"a` is not a plain word, so the line reds.
6. **Environment names.** Any non-comment occurrence of `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`, `VIRTUAL_ENV`
   or `--active` is a row: assignment, `:=` default, export, unset, or a mention. Measured: 0
   such lines on the real tree.
7. Delete the parser and the denylists: `_uv_segments`, `_uv_words`, `_uv_tokens`,
   `_uv_quoted_at`, `_uv_invocations`, `_uv_run_split`, `_uv_option_region`,
   `_uv_version_changes`, `_uv_hits`, `UV_SUBCOMMANDS`, `UV_GLOBAL_VALUED`, `UV_RUN_VALUED`,
   `UV_VERSION_SAFE_FLAGS`, `UV_MUTATING_VERBS`, `UV_PIP_MUTATING`, `UV_RUN_MUTATING_FLAGS`,
   `UV_ENV_RES`. Keep `uv_mutations(text)` as the public name of the per-text check, so the
   self-test calls stay simple.

The approved sets are module constants (for example `UV_APPROVED_FLAGS`,
`UV_APPROVED_VALUED`), so a new form is one reviewed edit plus a self-test row. The names are the
builder's call.

**The floor, without the parser.** The floor task passes when one invocation (rule 3) in a
non-comment line of its blob meets all of these:

- it is the first word of a logical line, or it follows `&&` or `;` outside quotes;
- it has `--isolated` and `--reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings` in its option region;
- its command is `pytest`, `python -m pytest` or `python3 -m pytest`.

The option order is free. A `uv run` that starts inside `echo '…'` gets no credit (the
existing row `a14_quoted` stays).

**The waivers.** Replace the 4 entries with the 27 lines from M6 (26 message or data lines plus
`ci/version-lockstep/run.sh:1635`), each with a one-line reason. The `uv lock` reason must say
that the line is in `run_write`, and that no Moon task passes `--write`. The builder derives the
final list from the real run, not from this spec, and the stale-entry rule keeps it exact.

### 4.3 Fixes that do not depend on the option

- G4 (UTF-8). A14 reads every script with `encoding="utf-8"`. Add `UnicodeDecodeError` to
  `INFRA_ERRORS`, so a script that is not UTF-8 gives rc 2 with a message that names the file.
  This also changes how A8 and A10 classify such a file (rc 2, not a traceback). It does not
  change what they follow.
- G5 (reachability). A14 gives a row for each file that it reads but that no input of
  `repo:affected-smoke` matches. Use the same match as A13 (`_moon_glob_re` over the task's
  `inputGlobs`, the `inputFiles` list, negated globs excluded). Measured: 0 rows on the real
  tree. Whether to share one helper with A13 is the builder's call. A13's rows must not change.

### 4.4 Accepted residuals (go into the README A14 entry)

- R1 (gap 6). A `source` word inside a quoted argument is followed. Fail-closed: at worst a false
  red or an infrastructure error. A correct fix needs a full shell parser.
- R2. uv through a variable, `eval` or a computed word is not seen (M5). Both options miss it.
- R3. A mutating command that `uv run` executes (`uv run pip install`,
  `uv run python -m pip install`) is not seen. The command word is not checked.
- R4. A direct write such as `py/.venv/bin/pip install` is not seen.
- R5. The existing limits stay: Moon toolchain actions (`InstallDependencies`) and the inexact
  relock of a plain `uv run` (SMA-765 R-toolchain, R-relock).
- R6. The cut in rule 3 is not quote-aware. A separator inside a quoted value ends the
  invocation early. The quote is then in an option-region word, which rule 5 reds. A quoted
  separator after the command word does not matter.

## 5. Self-test and proof

Every rule gets a self-test row. Every rule gets a mutation test: remove or neutralize the rule,
and at least one self-test row must fail. A mutation must compile and run. The builder records
the mutation results in the PR body.

### 5.1 Rows

- Keep the 47 red parser rows of today, unchanged.
- Keep the 14 rows of M7, with the expectation changed to red and a label that says "not an
  approved form".
- New red rows:
  - gap 1: `uv frobnicate --sync`;
  - gap 2: `echo ${VIRTUAL_ENV:=x}`, `: "${UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT:=.venv-x}"`;
  - gap 3: `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-x` with no command;
  - M5: `uv lock`, `uv run --upgrade pytest`, `uv tool install ruff`;
  - rule 3 and 5: `uv run --project "a b" --reinstall pytest`,
    `uv run --project $(x) --reinstall pytest`, `uv run --locked` (no command),
    `uv run --project=py pytest`, `uv build --wheel`, `bash -c "uv run --locked pytest; uv sync"`;
  - rule 1: `x # uv sync`;
  - rule 4: `uv run --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings pytest`.
- New green rows, one per form in M3:
  `uv build`; `uv run pytest`; `uv run --locked --project py python3 -c x`;
  `uv run --locked --project ci/release-plan --python '>=3.12' python3 x`;
  `uv run --project "$HERE" --python '>=3.12' python3 x`; `uv run --frozen python -c x`;
  `command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1`; the floor form; `touch a b && <floor form>`;
  `uv run \` + newline + `  --locked pytest` (a continuation); `# uv sync` (a full-line
  comment); `cat py/uv.lock`.
- Keep all check-level rows of today (task `env:`, followed `ci/` script, project script,
  `./` and `../` refs, the `source` closure rows, waiver reason and stale rows, the unreadable
  file rows, the floor rows, the quoted-floor row, the jq `. as $rows` row).
- New check-level rows:
  - G4: a scanned script with invalid UTF-8 raises an error that `INFRA_ERRORS` catches.
  - G5: a scanned script that no `repo:affected-smoke` input matches is a row. The fixture has
    a `repo` project with an `affected-smoke` task and its `inputGlobs`.

### 5.2 Real tree

- `python3 ci/affected-graph/cargo_moon_parity.py --self-test` passes.
- `/bin/bash ci/affected-graph/run.sh --negative-control` and `/bin/bash ci/affected-graph/run.sh`
  pass. Use system bash 3.2 on this Mac. Homebrew bash 5.3 deadlocks on a here-string over
  512 bytes.
- A14 gives 0 rows on the real tree, with the new waiver table.
- The real-tree negative control still exits 2 when the kernel task loses `--isolated`. Prove it
  once by hand: remove the flag in a scratch copy and run the parity script.
- `repo:ruff-ci` passes on the changed Python file (it needs bash 4+ locally).

## 6. Documentation

- `ci/affected-graph/README.md`, A14 entry: rewrite it for the allow-list rule (§4.2), G4, G5
  and the residuals R1-R6. Record each of the six SMA-768 gaps as closed or as a residual, with
  its number.
- The `Fix:` text of `a14` in `collect_findings`: say "use an approved form, or add the form to
  the allow-list with a self-test row; a line that only prints `uv` needs an
  `ALLOW_UV_ENV_SCRIPT` entry".
- Do not change the root `CLAUDE.md` or `ci/CLAUDE.md`.

## 7. Non-goals

- No change to any Moon task, `moon.yml` file or gate script. The tree is already green.
- No `--locked` on the plain `uv run` tasks (SMA-765 N2).
- No change to `SOURCE_STMT_RE`, `task_script_closure`, A8 or A10 (except the G4 error class).
- No full shell parser.

Anti-goal: an allow-list that is wide enough to pass the 14 synthetic forms of M7. That brings
the parser back under a new name.

## 8. Provisional calls — need Sven

- P1. **Option 2, not option 1** (§3). This is the main decision of the issue.
- P2. **27 waivers are acceptable** (C1, M6, M9). If Sven finds this too noisy, the fallback is
  option 1 with §4.3.
- P3. **Gap 3 is already closed.** The probes in M4 are red today. If Sven meant a different
  form, he must name it. Option 2 reds every non-comment mention of the two names (rule 6), so
  any form of an assignment is red.
- P4. **`uv lock` at `ci/version-lockstep/run.sh:1635` is waived, not moved.** No Moon task runs
  it today. The alternative is to move `run_write` out of the scanned script. That is a larger
  change to `repo:version-lockstep`.

## 9. Risks and rollback

- Risk: a waiver re-key on an unrelated edit of a message line (C1). The A14 message names the
  file, the line and the fix.
- Risk: a real new uv need reds A14 (C2). That is the intended behavior.

- Linear: SMA-768 (follows SMA-765, PR #457, merged as `8ef62d58`)
- Date: 2026-11-13
- Status: revision 1, for approval at GATE 1. The option decision (§3) is provisional. It needs
  Sven.

## 1. Intent

SMA-765 added check A14 to `repo:affected-smoke` (`check_uv_env_isolation` in
`ci/affected-graph/cargo_moon_parity.py`). A14 reds when a Moon task can change a uv project
environment in place. Six review rounds made A14 a small shell parser: a segmenter
(`_uv_segments`), a word splitter (`_uv_words`, `_uv_tokens`), a quote tracker (`_uv_quoted_at`),
a verb finder over a closed list (`UV_SUBCOMMANDS`, `UV_GLOBAL_VALUED`, `UV_RUN_VALUED`) and three
denylists (`UV_MUTATING_VERBS`, `UV_PIP_MUTATING`, `UV_RUN_MUTATING_FLAGS`). SMA-768 lists six
gaps that this parser leaves open, and asks for one decision:

- Option 1: close the gaps that matter in the current parser.
- Option 2: replace the parser with a smaller, blunter rule: an allow-list of exact approved `uv`
  forms.

This spec measures both options on the real tree and recommends option 2.

moon 2.5.3 and uv 0.11.16. The scripts are in the session scratch directory. They are not
committed.

  (`cargo_moon_parity.py:3225-3636`), 346 of them code. The waiver table
  `ALLOW_UV_ENV_SCRIPT` holds 4 entries. The self-test has a 61-row parser table and about 30
  check-level rows (`:6865-7070`, 206 lines).
- M2. **Scan scope today.** 171 Moon tasks have a command. A14 reads their blobs and 18 scripts
  (the `ci/**/*.sh` closure through `UV_SOURCE_STMT_RE`, plus `py/scripts/run_tests.sh`). On the
  real tree A14 gives 0 rows.
- M3. **Every executed `uv` form on the real tree.** There are 11 `uv` uses in task blobs and 17
  executed `uv` uses in the scanned scripts. They use 2 verbs and 5 options only:

  | Form | Where |
  |---|---|
  | `uv build` (no other word) | `paigasus-{kernel,ml,proto,workflows}-py:build` |
  | `uv run <cmd>` | `py:fmt`, `py:lint`, `py:typecheck` (3), `paigasus-gateway-conformance-py:test`, `py/scripts/run_tests.sh:17,32` (3) |
  | `uv run --isolated --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings pytest tests` | `paigasus-kernel-py:test` (the floor task) |
  | `uv run --locked --project <v> [--python <v>] <cmd>` | `ci/actionlint/run.sh:4619,4655,4669,5305,5982`, `ci/ruff/run.sh:90`, `ci/helm-render/run.sh:93`, `ci/wasm-lockstep/run.sh:52` |
  | `uv run --project <v> --python <v> <cmd>` | `ci/workflow-credentials/run.sh:33,70,78` |
  | `uv run --frozen <cmd>` | `ci/release-parity/ecosystems/python-semantic-release.sh:48` |
  | `uv lock` | `ci/version-lockstep/run.sh:1635`, inside `run_write`. `repo:version-lockstep` does not pass `--write`, so no Moon task runs this line. |

  | Gap | Probe | Today |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1. closed subcommand list | `uv frobnicate --sync` | green (missed) |

  | Probe | Today | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | `uv lock` | green | writes `py/uv.lock`. The SMA-768 issue text says that A14 covers `py/uv.lock`. It does not. |

  | `uv tool install ruff` | green | writes the uv tool directory, not a project environment |
  | `uv run pip install x` | green | can write `py/.venv` when pip is in it |
  | `UVB=uv; "$UVB" sync`, `$(printf u)v sync` | green | uv through a variable or a computed word |

  in M3 is green, except `uv lock` at `ci/version-lockstep/run.sh:1635`. 27 physical lines are
  red. 26 of them only name `uv` in a message, a `printf`, a `grep` pattern or Python data
  (for example `die_infra "uv is not on PATH …"` and `ws.get("tool", {}).get("uv", {})`). Of
  today's 4 waivers, 3 are among the 27. The fourth
  (`python-semantic-release.sh:34`) is a full-line comment, which option 2 does not scan, so it
  goes away. So the waiver table grows from 4 to 27 entries: 26 message or data lines and the
  `uv lock` line.

  because they are not an approved form: the six `uv version` rows,
  `uv run --isolated --force-reinstall pytest`, `uv --directory sync run pytest`, four
  `--isolated` rows with an option or package that is not approved, `echo uv run's own status`,
  and `touch a b && uv run --isolated --reinstall-package p pytest tests` (`p` is not
  `paigasus-py-bindings`). None of the 14 forms occurs on the real tree.

  task. The prototype gives a row for `paigasus-kernel-py:test`
